$comment: Dim sum release code-name ledger for WinSCP Material.
Every build carries a dim sum code name (dish English name + Traditional
Chinese) beside its version number. The code name labels the build; it never
replaces the version, which stays the thing users and machines identify a
build by.
HOW ASSIGNMENT WORKS, AND WHY IT IS AUDITABLE WITHOUT A PUSH.
CI must not push back to this repository (that would retrigger itself), so
the mapping is not appended here by a workflow. Instead it is DETERMINISTIC:
`order` below is the fixed sequence, and release number N (the GitHub
Actions run number, which is monotonic) takes order[N - 1]. Anyone can
recompute the whole mapping from this file with:
node build/pick-codename.js --index <N>
Each release also carries the assignment in three places a reader can check
without trusting CI: the release notes, a codename.json release asset, and
the workflow run summary.
USED ONCE PER RELEASE. A dish is never reused. The bundled catalog is still
being filled in (design/winscp-data.js reports the verified dishes), so when
the sequence is exhausted the release ships with its version alone and the
notes say so plainly, rather than recycling a name and making two builds
indistinguishable.
ONLY DISHES WITH A REAL BUNDLED IMAGE ARE ELIGIBLE. build/pick-codename.js
decodes the PNG before offering a dish; a record whose image is missing or
does not decode is skipped, never guessed at, and never substituted.
